faq.description: Answers to common questions about the 30HD0D engine in the Land Rover Discovery 4. If yours is not covered, our team can help.

faqs.q: How do 30HD0D, 306DT and 30DDTX engines differ for Discovery 4?
faqs.a: They belong to the same 3.0 V6 diesel family but can differ in emissions equipment, calibration and ancillaries by model year. We check your VIN and engine code before recommending a compatible replacement.

faqs.q: How do used, reconditioned and rebuilt 30HD0D engines compare?
faqs.a: A used engine comes from a donor vehicle, a reconditioned engine is stripped and given new wear parts, and a rebuild restores your existing engine. We recommend an option after assessing the fault and vehicle.

faqs.q: Can I buy a Discovery 4 30HD0D engine supply only?
faqs.a: Yes. Trade buyers, independent garages and private customers with their own mechanic can buy supply only. Alternatively, choose supply and fit and our technicians will install the engine at our Grays, Essex workshop.

faqs.q: What affects the Discovery 4 engine replacement cost for a 30HD0D?
faqs.a: The cost depends on the engine option, the condition of your current engine, any parts needed such as turbos or a DPF, and the labour involved, including body lifting. Send your registration or VIN for a quote.

faqs.q: Is there a warranty on a replacement 30HD0D engine?
faqs.a: Warranty cover depends on the engine option and whether we carry out the installation. We confirm the exact terms in writing with your quote, so you know what is covered before work begins.

faqs.q: Do you deliver Land Rover 3.0 TDV6 engines across the UK?
faqs.a: Yes. We deliver engines throughout the United Kingdom from our Grays workshop. Delivery arrangements and costs are confirmed in your quote, and supply and fit customers can bring their Discovery to us.

faqs.q: How long does a 30HD0D engine replacement usually take?
faqs.a: The timescale depends on engine availability, whether a rebuild is needed, any body-lift work and additional repairs found during inspection. We give you an estimated timeframe with your quote and keep you informed.

workshopIntro.title: Repair, Rebuild or Replace Your 30HD0D?
workshopIntro.description: The fault, mileage and value of your Discovery 4 decide the best route. Glow plug, turbo, DPF and oil cooler faults can often be repaired individually. If the bearings have failed or the crankshaft is damaged, a rebuild or Land Rover Discovery 4 30HD0D engine replacement is usually the more dependable choice.
paragraphs: Bottom-end damage is often linked to oil supply or contamination, so we investigate beyond the engine itself. Where relevant, we inspect the oil cooler, turbos, intercooler, EGR, DPF and cooling system, and renew the oil, filters and coolant before the engine runs.

Send your registration or VIN with a short description of the symptoms. We will confirm compatibility, explain the options and quote for supply only, supply and fit at our Grays workshop, or delivery across the UK.

engineProblems.title: Common Discovery 4 30HD0D Faults
engineProblems.description: This 3.0 V6 diesel usually shows warning signs early, so prompt checks can prevent wider engine damage.

cards.title: Main Bearing Wear and Crank Damage
cards.description: A rumbling or knocking noise, oil pressure warnings or a sudden loss of power may indicate main bearing wear and possible crankshaft damage. We check oil pressure and bottom-end condition.

cards.title: Cam and Pump Belt Failure Risk
cards.description: The engine relies on belts to drive the camshafts and high-pressure fuel pump. Overdue belts or worn tensioners can fail without warning. We inspect both belt drives and their tensioners.

cards.title: Secondary Turbo Not Engaging
cards.description: Flat performance at higher revs, boost fault codes or limp mode may point to a secondary turbo, valve or actuator fault in the twin-turbo system. We test both turbos and their controls.
cards.action: Fuel rail and injector leak-off test

cards.title: Leaking Oil Cooler Seals
cards.description: A milky film under the cap, oil traces in the coolant or a falling coolant level may come from a leaking oil cooler or seal. We check the fluids and pressure-test the system.

cards.title: Glow Plug and Cold-Start Faults
cards.description: Long cranking times, rough running when cold or glow plug warnings may be caused by failed glow plugs or a faulty glow plug control module. We test the glow plugs and their circuit.

cards.title: Exhaust Soot and DPF Faults
cards.description: DPF warning lights, frequent regenerations or reduced power may follow short journeys, EGR problems or sensor faults that stop the filter clearing. We read soot data and assess the DPF.

engineOverview.title: Land Rover Discovery 4 30HD0D Engine: Your Complete 3.0 V6 Diesel Guide
paragraphs: The Land Rover Discovery 4 30HD0D engine is a version of the 3.0-litre twin-turbo V6 diesel, used in TDV6 and SDV6 Discovery 4 models as well as other Land Rover vehicles. Many are now high-mileage, and bearing wear, belt neglect, turbo faults and DPF problems often lead owners to seek repair or replacement.

The Land Rover 3.0 TDV6 engine family includes several codes, such as 306DT, 30DDTX and 30HD0D, with differences in emissions equipment, calibration and ancillaries. We identify the correct Discovery 4 engine by checking your VIN, engine code and registration.

Whether you need a targeted repair, an engine rebuild or a complete Land Rover Discovery 4 30HD0D engine replacement, our team assesses the vehicle and explains each option. Call us or send your registration for a written quote.
